title: External World and Open-System Effects
results: Open systems contain independently changing actors and state outside Runtime authority.
An External Effect is an externally owned visible change, obligation or state transition rather than a local function return.
Intent, request, transport, provider acceptance, provider operation, external transition, observation/receipt, reconciliation and semantic outcome are distinct stages.
Missing response cannot prove provider rejection or non-occurrence.
Caller knowledge and provider Reality are independent axes; committed provider state can coexist with caller unknown.
External idempotency requires provider-side durable binding/equivalence and retention; a caller key alone is insufficient.
Runtime replay lifetime and provider deduplication/evidence lifetime are distinct.
Asynchronous providers separate request acceptance from terminal Effect completion through provider operation identities and state machines.
Provider operation identity, external resource identity, client effect key and Runtime Operation identity are distinct namespaces.
Resource identity, readiness and current state are distinct facts.
Generic Runtime execution terminality remains separate from arbitrary external Effect terminality.
deliveryDisposition=committed is Runtime physical-result certainty rather than external or domain completion.
Process exit zero/nonzero cannot generically prove external Effect success/absence.
A receipt must be scoped to the exact provider frontier/fact it proves; acceptance and completion receipts are distinct.
Provider receipts remain narrower than Semantic Goal completion.
External observations require authority plus freshness/version; a correct historical observation can be stale now.
Eventual consistency can make post-write absence insufficient evidence of effect non-occurrence.
Reconciliation is evidence-based convergence of local knowledge with provider truth and is distinct from retry.
Identity-bound provider query is stronger than heuristic search for recovery.
Current external resource state does not reconstruct complete causal history when other actors can mutate it.
Finance order state demonstrates first-class partial Effects such as partial fills and canceled orders with committed fills.
Cancel and compensation are new external actions that can race existing effects.
Cloud providers demonstrate accepted, in-progress, success, failure and cancellation state machines that outlive the initiating request.
SMTP demonstrates responsibility acceptance, technical delivery and human semantic outcome as separate frontiers.
Action Authority, Observation Authority and Semantic Authority may belong to different owners.
Webhook or callback delivery is an observation/event channel; notification duplication/loss differs from underlying Effect duplication/loss.
Provider versions, generations and event IDs strengthen ordering, preconditions and reconciliation but remain provider-scoped.
Runtime Release and Workspace Patch justify owner-specific structured Effect contracts rather than a universal Runtime Effect kernel.
Generic workspace.exec must remain effect-opaque because Runtime does not own arbitrary provider state machines, IDs, receipts or reconciliation semantics.
Host/domain remains the semantic convergence and policy owner across Runtime Operations and provider observations.
Permanent epistemic unknown is legitimate when authoritative historical evidence expired or never existed.
The governing law is ExternalEffectClaimScope <= ProviderOwnedEvidenceAndControlScope.

nextRound.title: Cross-Domain Falsification and Runtime Foundations v1 Reconstruction
nextRound.entryQuestion: When RF0-RF15 are attacked as one theory across local, distributed, adversarial, nondeterministic and external-world cases, which distinctions survive strongly enough to freeze as the minimal Runtime Foundations v1?

notes: RF15 explains open-system Effect boundaries but does not authorize generic external adapters, automatic retry, webhook infrastructure, finance/cloud/payment/email integrations, compensation engines or production API changes.
